title: Let's Do Math
text: Each derby car weight 5oz (141.748 grams), or it's supposed to. Each car is lifted to the begining of the track at a height of ~ 1.5 meters. We can use the equation for potential energy mass*gravity*height to get the inital energy of the car to calculate that each car has about (.141*1.5*9.8) = 2 jouls of energy. If we assume that the car converts half of its energy to kinetic energy we can get a final speed with the kinetic energy equation of 1/2 mass * velocity squared. So 1J = .5 * .141 v^2, sqrt(1/(.5*.141)) = 3.7m/s. FUN!
